pitch: Why competent people jointly make decisions contrary to their goal, and persist: errors of reasoning, of groups and of meaning.
br: contrary to the goal · persistence · good faith
When action detaches from the goal
quiz: What is an absurd decision according to Morel?
An action radically contrary to the goal pursued, and persistent
Those who make them are often competent and acting in good faith.
What data error played a role in the Challenger accident?
Looking only at flights with incidents, which hid the link with cold
Across all flights, the link was obvious.
A group decides on something nobody wanted, each believing they're pleasing the others
Everyone keeps their opinion, but keeps it to themselves.
What does “reversing the burden of proof” mean?
Demanding proof that an action is dangerous rather than proof that it is safe
Proof is required to stop, not to continue.
What is a wrong frame of reference?
A false mental model through which all information is interpreted
It explains why absurd decisions persist.
Continuing to invest in a failed project because of what has already been committed
Sunk costs push us to keep spending.
Collegiality, no punishment for reported errors, the right to stop
Aviation, nuclear power and submarines are examples.
Which question helps break out of escalation?
How much have we already spent?
If we hadn't spent anything yet, would we launch this project today?
It neutralizes the effect of costs already committed.
